control_blender_ui.name: control_blender_ui
control_blender_ui.title: Control Blender Ui
control_blender_ui.description: Perform a named agent_control action in the explicitly attached Blender window. Use inspect for editor IDs, active tool, Properties tabs, shared workspace and agent cursors. Actions display labelled agent pointers; move_cursor moves this overlay, never the OS cursor. Use observe after an external screenshot to show a brief eye badge and viewport pulse. Before set_tool on a shared workspace, use isolate_workspace then inspect for new editor IDs. Uses Blender UI APIs, not physical key/click events or arbitrary button lookup. Requires attached mode; does not launch Blender or execute arbitrary scripts.

agent_control.description: inspect, observe, move_cursor, clear_cursor, open_menu, select_object, set_tool, show_properties, set_property or isolate_workspace.

target.description: Menu add/object/view, tool select_box/move/rotate/scale, object name, Properties tab such as OBJECT, or active-object property location/rotation_euler/scale.

area_id.description: Editor ID from inspect; required for editor actions with multiple matches. Object selection/property writes do not require it. Re-inspect after workspace isolation.

position.description: move_cursor only: agent overlay coordinates [x, y] in [0, 1], bottom-left origin; default center.

value.description: set_property only: three finite values for the active object; rotation_euler is XYZ radians, written in the object's rotation mode (quaternion, axis-angle, other order).

agent_id.description: Visible agent label, 1 to 64 printable characters; defaults to the MCP session identity. Use distinct stable labels for named agents across connections. clear_cursor removes only this agent's marker in the attached window; markers expire after 120 seconds.

get_blender_info.name: get_blender_info
get_blender_info.title: Get Blender Info
get_blender_info.description: Get information about the active Blender runtime.

attach_blender_window.name: attach_blender_window
attach_blender_window.title: Attach Blender Window
attach_blender_window.description: Attached mode: select the Blender process and window that Blender tools act on, the same as `simul blender attach`. Use it to recover after another file was loaded (read_homefile, open_mainfile) or Blender restarted. Succeeds only when the choice is unambiguous; pass instance_id/window_id from the error details or get_blender_info otherwise.

instance_id.description: Bridge instance ID; required when several Blender processes run.

window_id.description: Window ID; required when the selected process has several windows.

list_blender_scene_objects.name: list_blender_scene_objects
list_blender_scene_objects.title: List Blender Scene Objects
list_blender_scene_objects.description: List objects from the active Blender scene, a page at a time: count objects from offset, total matching, and next_offset for the next page (null after the last). A page stops before its entries pass 30000 bytes of JSON, so it can hold fewer than max_items. Each entry names a collection holding the object.

max_items.description: Maximum number of objects to return.

offset.description: How many matching objects to skip, as next_offset gives it.

get_blender_object_info.name: get_blender_object_info
get_blender_object_info.title: Get Blender Object Info
get_blender_object_info.description: Get detailed information about a single Blender object. location, rotation_euler (XYZ radians) and scale are its own transform, relative to its parent as Blender's Location, Rotation and Scale fields show them; world_location, world_rotation_euler, world_rotation_quaternion, world_scale and matrix_world give where it is in the scene. rotation_mode says how Blender stores the rotation (rotation_in_mode); rotation_quaternion gives it as a quaternion.

get_blender_mesh_info.name: get_blender_mesh_info
get_blender_mesh_info.title: Get Blender Mesh Info
get_blender_mesh_info.description: Get a Blender mesh object's vertex, edge, face and triangle counts: of the stored mesh, and evaluated with the modifiers enabled in the viewport, which is what an export writes. A mesh in Edit Mode is counted with its unsaved edits. warnings name modifiers set differently for render, which USD export evaluates.

get_blender_bounding_box.name: get_blender_bounding_box
get_blender_bounding_box.title: Get Blender Bounding Box
get_blender_bounding_box.description: Get the bounding box of a Blender object.

world_space.description: Return corners in world space when True.

search_blender_objects.name: search_blender_objects
search_blender_objects.title: Search Blender Objects
search_blender_objects.description: Search for objects in the Blender scene by name pattern or type (in any case), a page at a time as list_blender_scene_objects pages: count, total and next_offset.

name_pattern.description: Python regular expression searched for in each object name; a repeated group that holds a quantifier or alternatives, as in (\w+)+, is refused because it can run for hours.

object_type.description: Blender object type filter (MESH, LIGHT, etc.), in any case.

offset.description: How many matching objects to skip, as next_offset gives it.

summarize_blender_scene.name: summarize_blender_scene
summarize_blender_scene.title: Summarize Blender Scene
summarize_blender_scene.description: Get a high-level summary of the Blender scene: object counts by type, its top-level collections, active camera and frame range.

get_blender_material_info.name: get_blender_material_info
get_blender_material_info.title: Get Blender Material Info
get_blender_material_info.description: Get a Blender material's Principled BSDF values and what drives them: an input a link drives reads null in principled_params, and linked_inputs names its source node and, for an image texture (also behind a Normal Map node), the image file, colour space and packing. Lists at most max_nodes nodes, those feeding the output first, with node_count for the whole tree.

get_blender_distance_between.name: get_blender_distance_between
get_blender_distance_between.title: Get Blender Distance Between
get_blender_distance_between.description: Measure the Euclidean distance between two Blender objects.

check_blender_object_bounds.name: check_blender_object_bounds
check_blender_object_bounds.title: Check Blender Object Bounds
check_blender_object_bounds.description: Check where a Blender object's world-space bounding box lies relative to an axis-aligned box: relation 'inside' (within_bounds), 'intersecting' or 'outside'. The bounding box turns and scales with the object; origin_within_bounds tests the origin alone. bounds_min must not exceed bounds_max.

object_name.description: Name of the Blender object to test.

bounds_min.description: Minimum corner of the box as [x, y, z] in scene units (Blender is Z-up).

bounds_max.description: Maximum corner of the box as [x, y, z] in scene units.

capture_blender_viewport.name: capture_blender_viewport
capture_blender_viewport.title: Capture Blender Viewport
capture_blender_viewport.description: Capture Blender as a JPEG. In attached mode the default (method='auto') is the 3D View the user sees: view angle, shading, overlays, Edit Mode and unsaved edits, with no camera needed, keeping the view's aspect ratio within width x height (capture_method viewport; an external engine's Rendered view, such as Cycles, is read from the screen as viewport_screen and includes overlapping UI). Embedded (headless bpy) mode has no 3D View, so 'auto' renders. method='render' renders through the scene camera, or through a temporary camera removed afterwards: aligned to the 3D View when attached, framing the visible objects when embedded or when the window shows no 3D View (render_temp_camera_view / render_temp_camera_framing). camera_name captures through that camera without changing the scene camera or the view: a render renders through it, a viewport capture draws the 3D View's shading from it (viewport_camera). The image arrives as an MCP image content block, followed by a JSON block with success, width, height, engine, capture_method, camera_name, format and image_attached=true. In attached mode, briefly show an agent eye badge and border pulse after success. Agent annotations are excluded from the captured image.

width.description: Maximum image width in pixels. A viewport capture, or a render through a temporary camera aligned to the 3D View, keeps the view's aspect ratio inside width x height; other renders are exactly width x height.

height.description: Maximum image height in pixels; see width.

method.description: "viewport": the 3D View as the user sees it (view angle, shading, overlays, Edit Mode, unsaved changes); attached mode only. "render": a render through the scene camera, or through a temporary camera when the scene has none (aligned to the 3D View when attached, framing the visible objects otherwise), removed afterwards. "auto" (default): "viewport" when attached, "render" in embedded mode.

agent_id.description: Visible capture feedback label in attached mode; ignored in embedded mode.

camera_name.description: Capture through this camera instead of the scene camera or the 3D View's angle; the scene camera and the view are left as they were. A render renders through it; a viewport capture draws the 3D View's shading from it (capture_method viewport_camera), keeping the render's aspect ratio inside width x height.

set_blender_camera_view.name: set_blender_camera_view
set_blender_camera_view.title: Set Blender Camera View
set_blender_camera_view.description: Place a Blender camera (the active one by default) at a world-space location and XYZ Euler rotation, whatever its parent and rotation mode. Success means the placement is in the camera's transform; its constraints (Track To, Copy Location, Child Of, ...) still apply and are never muted. location and rotation_euler report where Blender evaluates the camera; placement_overridden is true when that is not the request, with constraints_applied and a warning on how to disable them. Keys on the camera's transform take over at the next frame change. Blender's viewport skips a camera disabled in viewports unless it is needed by something visible, or is the scene camera or a timeline marker's camera and its hide_viewport is not animated: when Blender did not evaluate it after the placement (or its evaluated pose did not change), override_check is 'skipped' and placement_overridden null.

rotation_euler.description: World-space camera rotation [rx, ry, rz] in radians, as an XYZ Euler.

camera_name.description: Target camera name. Uses active camera when None.

get_blender_camera_info.name: get_blender_camera_info
get_blender_camera_info.title: Get Blender Camera Info
get_blender_camera_info.description: Get a Blender camera's world-space location and XYZ Euler rotation where Blender evaluates it (constraints included), the constraints that act on it (constraints_applied), lens and clip range (the active camera by default). Blender keeps a stale pose for a camera disabled in viewports unless it is needed by something visible through a child, a constraint or a modifier, or is the scene camera or a timeline marker's camera and its hide_viewport is not animated: its pose is then composed from its own transform (pose_source 'transform'), without its constraints, drivers and keys, and warning says what that leaves out.

camera_name.description: Target camera name. Uses active camera when None.

focus_blender_on_object.name: focus_blender_on_object
focus_blender_on_object.title: Focus Blender On Object
focus_blender_on_object.description: Frame a Blender object with a camera (the active one by default): aim it from the front and above at the object's bounding-box center, at the distance where the object fits the frame (an orthographic camera gets the ortho_scale that fits it), widening the clip range when it would cut the object away. As with set_blender_camera_view, success means the framing is in the camera's transform and its constraints still apply: camera_location and camera_rotation_euler report where Blender evaluates the camera, and placement_overridden is true when constraints or drivers moved it off the framing. For a camera disabled in viewports that Blender did not evaluate after the placement (or whose evaluated pose did not change), override_check is 'skipped' and placement_overridden null.

distance_factor.description: Multiple of the framing distance (of ortho_scale for an orthographic camera): 1.0 fits the object's bounding sphere in the frame with 5% to spare, 2.0 shows the object at half that size, and below 1.0 crops it.

camera_name.description: Target camera name. Uses active camera when None.

get_blender_viewport_info.name: get_blender_viewport_info
get_blender_viewport_info.title: Get Blender Viewport Info
get_blender_viewport_info.description: Get the render settings (engine, resolution, film, active camera) and, in attached mode, view3d: the 3D View captures use, with its view_matrix, eye_location, perspective, lens, clip range and shading. view3d is null without an editor window (embedded bpy, blender -b) or 3D View, and view3d_unavailable_reason says which.

capture_blender_viewport_sequence.name: capture_blender_viewport_sequence
capture_blender_viewport_sequence.title: Capture Blender Viewport Sequence
capture_blender_viewport_sequence.description: Capture a frame range as JPEG files, each made like capture_blender_viewport with the same method and camera_name (the 3D View when attached, a camera render in embedded mode), and return their paths: frames [{frame, file_path}], output_dir (default a new folder in the sandbox's capture directory), width and height. end_frame must not be before start_frame. One call captures at most max_frames (default 50, at most 100) and starts no frame after 10 s, since Blender is busy meanwhile; then complete is false and next_start_frame says where to continue. In attached mode, briefly show an agent eye badge and border pulse after success. Agent annotations are excluded from the captured images.

end_frame.description: Last frame to capture (inclusive); not before start_frame.

width.description: Maximum image width, as for capture_blender_viewport.

height.description: Maximum image height, as for capture_blender_viewport.

agent_id.description: Visible capture feedback label in attached mode; ignored in embedded mode.

camera_name.description: Capture through this camera, as for capture_blender_viewport.

output_dir.description: Folder for the frame files, inside the sandbox; created when missing, and existing frame files of the same numbers are replaced. Default: a new sequence-<time>-<id> folder in the capture directory.

max_frames.description: Most frames captured by this call, 1 to 100.

create_blender_object.name: create_blender_object
create_blender_object.title: Create Blender Object
create_blender_object.description: Create a new object in the Blender scene's active collection, or in the scene's own collection when the active one is excluded, hidden or disabled in viewports (warning says so). It stays in Object Mode whatever Blender's Enter Edit Mode preference.

object_type.description: Type key (CUBE, SPHERE, POINT_LIGHT, CAMERA, etc.).

delete_blender_object.name: delete_blender_object
delete_blender_object.title: Delete Blender Object
delete_blender_object.description: Delete an object from the current Blender scene with Blender's own Delete, which also resets a rigid body's cache. Another scene linking it keeps it (remaining_scenes); use_global=true deletes it from every scene and the file.

object_name.description: Name of the object to delete.

use_global.description: Delete it from every scene and the file, not only from the current scene.

set_blender_object_mode.name: set_blender_object_mode
set_blender_object_mode.title: Set Blender Object Mode
set_blender_object_mode.description: Switch an object (the active one by default) into a mode, as the 3D View's mode menu does: OBJECT by default, the way back for a window left in Edit or Pose Mode, where create, delete, import and the other mode-sensitive tools refuse to run.

mode.description: OBJECT (default), EDIT, POSE, SCULPT, VERTEX_PAINT, WEIGHT_PAINT, TEXTURE_PAINT or another mode Blender's object.mode_set takes, in any case.

object_name.description: The object to switch; the active object by default.

set_blender_object_transform.name: set_blender_object_transform
set_blender_object_transform.title: Set Blender Object Transform
set_blender_object_transform.description: Set location, rotation, and/or scale of a Blender object's own transform, relative to its parent (Blender's Location, Rotation and Scale fields). rotation_euler is XYZ Euler radians, or pass rotation_quaternion [w, x, y, z] instead; either is converted to the object's rotation_mode (glTF imports store quaternions), which is kept. The reply reports the result, rotation_mode and world_location.

location.description: New location [x, y, z] relative to the parent, or None to keep current.

rotation_euler.description: New rotation as XYZ Euler angles [rx, ry, rz] in radians, converted to the object's rotation_mode; None to keep current.

scale.description: New scale [sx, sy, sz] or None to keep current.

rotation_quaternion.description: New rotation as a quaternion [w, x, y, z], normalized and converted to the object's rotation_mode; instead of rotation_euler.

set_blender_object_parent.name: set_blender_object_parent
set_blender_object_parent.title: Set Blender Object Parent
set_blender_object_parent.description: Parent one Blender object to another. By default the child keeps its world transform, as Blender's Parent > Object (Keep Transform); keep_transform=false makes its own values relative to the parent, so it moves. A parent that is the child itself or one of its descendants is refused.

keep_transform.description: Keep the child's world transform (default); false clears the parent inverse, so the child's own values become relative to the parent and it moves.

clear_blender_object_parent.name: clear_blender_object_parent
clear_blender_object_parent.title: Clear Blender Object Parent
clear_blender_object_parent.description: Remove parent from a Blender object.

assign_blender_material.name: assign_blender_material
assign_blender_material.title: Assign Blender Material
assign_blender_material.description: Assign a Principled BSDF material to a Blender object. A material of that name is reused (repeating the call changes nothing more; reuse_existing=false creates a new one), and shading arguments left out keep the material's values, so an existing material can be assigned as it is. By default it replaces the object's material: slot 0, every face. slot_index puts it in one slot (the slot count adds one); face_indices assigns it to those faces only. link='OBJECT' puts it in this object's slot instead of the mesh's, but faces and the slot count belong to the mesh: on mesh data other objects share, changing them is refused unless single_user=true gives this object its own copy first (in Object Mode). base_color is RGB or RGBA in 0-1; alpha below 1 sets the Principled Alpha and blended rendering (exported as USD opacity). Image textures can drive base color, metallic, roughness and normal (they need a UV map: uv_unwrap_blender_mesh); an image already in the file keeps its colour space, and an input reading it differently gets its own copy. Blender's USD exporter writes UsdPreviewSurface; it does not write OmniPBR or MDL. Everything is checked first; a failure leaves nothing behind.

object_name.description: Object to assign the material to (mesh, curve, text, or another type with material slots).

base_color.description: RGB or RGBA in [0, 1]; the alpha becomes the Principled Alpha, and below 1 the material renders blended.

slot_index.description: Slot to put the material in; the slot count adds one.

face_indices.description: Mesh faces to assign the material to.

link.description: DATA (the mesh's slot, shared by linked duplicates) or OBJECT (this object's slot).

single_user.description: Give this object its own copy of shared data first, so the change leaves the objects sharing it alone.

reuse_existing.description: Reuse a material of that name when one exists.

base_color_texture.description: Image file driving Base Color (in the colour space Blender loads it in: sRGB, or linear for float images).

normal_texture.description: Tangent-space normal map image (Non-Color), through a Normal Map node.

add_blender_modifier.name: add_blender_modifier
add_blender_modifier.title: Add Blender Modifier
add_blender_modifier.description: Add a modifier to a Blender mesh, curve or other object with a modifier stack. params are the modifier's settings by Blender RNA name, checked before use: an unknown name is refused with the closest names, an enum value must be one of its items, a number must lie within the setting's limits (Blender would clamp it silently), and an object or collection setting takes its name, e.g. {'object': 'Cutter'} for BOOLEAN. The reply echoes the stored settings. A refused call leaves no modifier behind. DECIMATE is refused on a mesh with invalid geometry, which can freeze Blender; run clean_blender_mesh first.

params.description: Modifier settings by RNA name, e.g. {"ratio": 0.5} for DECIMATE or {"object": "Cutter"} for BOOLEAN.

apply_blender_modifier.name: apply_blender_modifier
apply_blender_modifier.title: Apply Blender Modifier
apply_blender_modifier.description: Apply one modifier of a Blender mesh object, baking its result into the mesh data (for example a Decimate before export) and removing it from the stack. A modifier below others is applied to the base mesh without them, with a warning; shared mesh data is copied for this object first. A modifier disabled in the viewport is refused, as Blender would drop it unapplied. Requires Object Mode.

modifier_name.description: Name of the modifier to apply.

remove_blender_modifier.name: remove_blender_modifier
remove_blender_modifier.title: Remove Blender Modifier
remove_blender_modifier.description: Remove one modifier from a Blender object's stack without applying it.

modifier_name.description: Name of the modifier to remove.

set_blender_light_params.name: set_blender_light_params
set_blender_light_params.title: Set Blender Light Params
set_blender_light_params.description: Set a Blender light's parameters, optionally changing its type first (light_type). Each setting must belong to the light's type: shadow_soft_size is the radius of POINT and SPOT lights, spot_size and spot_blend are SPOT's, angle is a SUN's softness, and shape, size and size_y are an AREA light's; others are refused, as are values outside Blender's limits (which it would clamp silently) and negative energy. The reply echoes every setting of the light's type as stored.

energy.description: Light power in watts (irradiance in W/m² for SUN), >= 0.

color.description: Light color RGB [r, g, b], each >= 0.

spot_size.description: Spot cone angle in radians, 1 degree to pi (SPOT).

shadow_soft_size.description: Light radius for soft shadows, >= 0 (POINT, SPOT).

light_type.description: Change the light to POINT, SUN, SPOT or AREA first.

angle.description: Sun's angular diameter in radians, 0 to pi (SUN).

size.description: Area light size, >= 0 (AREA; its width for RECTANGLE and ELLIPSE).

size_y.description: Area light height, >= 0 (AREA with shape RECTANGLE or ELLIPSE).

shape.description: Area light shape: SQUARE, RECTANGLE, DISK or ELLIPSE (AREA).

open_blender_file.name: open_blender_file
open_blender_file.title: Open Blender File
open_blender_file.description: Open a .blend file, replacing the current scene. Refuses with UnsavedChangesError while the open file has unsaved changes (in attached mode every agent edit counts, as each is an undo step); save them first with save_blender_file, or pass discard_unsaved=true to discard them.

discard_unsaved.description: Open even though the current file has unsaved changes, which are then lost. To keep them, save first with save_blender_file.

save_blender_file.name: save_blender_file
save_blender_file.title: Save Blender File
save_blender_file.description: Save the current .blend file, in place or under a new .blend path, which then becomes the open document. Other extensions are refused; use export_blender_file for other formats.

file_path.description: Path of the .blend file to save to. None saves in place.

import_blender_file.name: import_blender_file
import_blender_file.title: Import Blender File
import_blender_file.description: Import an OBJ, FBX, glTF, USD, STL or PLY file into the Blender scene, optionally scaled about the world origin (scale). The textures, buffers, MTL libraries and USD layers it would read must be inside the sandbox too, or it is refused with SandboxError; within the sandbox the FBX importer does not search folders for textures.

file_format.description: One of OBJ, FBX, GLTF, USD, STL, PLY.

scale.description: Uniform scale applied to the imported objects about the world origin (1.0 keeps them as the file has them). OBJ, FBX, STL and PLY pass it to Blender's importer as global_scale. For glTF and USD the imported root objects' location and scale are multiplied by it: Blender's glTF importer has no such option, and Blender 5.0.1's USD importer ignored its own for a USD file Blender wrote. Keys or a Transform Cache constraint on such a root's transform take over again at the next frame change, and warning names those roots.

export_blender_file.name: export_blender_file
export_blender_file.title: Export Blender File
export_blender_file.description: Export the scene, the selection (selected_only), a list of objects (object_names) or a collection (collection_name) to OBJ, FBX, glTF, USD, STL or PLY. file_path must end in the format's extension and is written exactly: for GLTF, .glb writes a GLB and .gltf a .gltf with its .bin and textures (gltf_format to choose GLTF_EMBEDDED). Modifiers are applied and animation included by default (apply_modifiers, export_animation, frame_start/frame_end; USD animation is on here although Blender's exporter leaves it off). FBX, OBJ, STL and PLY take axis_forward/axis_up and global_scale; USD takes usd_up_axis, meters_per_unit and root_prim_path. Missing folders are created, Edit Mode is entered again afterwards, an unrelated existing .bin/.mtl beside the file is not replaced unless overwrite_companion_files, and files_written lists every file written.

file_path.description: Path to export to, ending in .obj, .fbx, .glb or .gltf, .usd/.usda/.usdc/.usdz, .stl or .ply for the format.

file_format.description: One of OBJ, FBX, GLTF, USD, STL, PLY.

selected_only.description: Export only the selected objects; an error when none is selected.

object_names.description: Export exactly these objects (children are not added). They are selected for the export and the previous selection is restored afterwards. Not with selected_only or collection_name.

collection_name.description: Export the objects of this collection and its child collections that are in the view layer, the same way.

apply_modifiers.description: Export the meshes with their modifiers applied (default, for every format). USD always applies them, except that Blender writes a last Subdivision Surface as a USD subdivision scheme, so false is an error for USD.

export_animation.description: Include animation (default): glTF actions, FBX baked animation, USD time samples over the scene's frame range. Blender's USD exporter leaves animation out unless asked; this default includes it. OBJ, STL and PLY have no animation.

frame_start.description: First frame of the exported animation (glTF, FBX, USD), with frame_end; the scene's frame range is restored afterwards. Without them FBX and USD use the scene's frame range and glTF each action's whole range.

frame_end.description: Last frame of the exported animation, with frame_start.

gltf_format.description: GLB (one binary .glb), GLTF_SEPARATE (.gltf plus .bin and textures beside it) or GLTF_EMBEDDED (one .gltf with its data inline). Default: GLB for .glb and GLTF_SEPARATE for .gltf; it must agree with the extension.

axis_forward.description: FBX, OBJ, STL and PLY: the axis written as forward, one of X, Y, Z, -X, -Y, -Z, together with axis_up on another axis. Default: the exporter's (FBX and OBJ -Z forward, Y up; STL and PLY Y forward, Z up).

axis_up.description: The axis written as up, together with axis_forward.

global_scale.description: FBX, OBJ, STL and PLY: scale factor applied to the exported data (default 1.0).

usd_up_axis.description: USD: the stage's up axis, Y (Blender rotates the scene from Z-up to Y-up) or Z (default, Blender's own).

meters_per_unit.description: USD: the stage's metersPerUnit (default 1.0); Blender scales the root so objects keep their size. Blender 4.4 and later.

root_prim_path.description: USD: path of the prim everything is exported under (default /root); an empty string exports without one.

overwrite_companion_files.description: Let the export replace an existing .bin (GLTF_SEPARATE) or .mtl (OBJ) beside file_path that the file at file_path does not refer to. file_path itself is always replaced.

get_blender_file_info.name: get_blender_file_info
get_blender_file_info.title: Get Blender File Info
get_blender_file_info.description: Get information about the current .blend file: its path, saved and dirty state, the current scene's name and object_count, and file_object_count for the whole file.

frame.description: Frame number to set, within -1048574..1048574 (Blender's limits).

get_blender_frame.name: get_blender_frame
get_blender_frame.title: Get Blender Frame
get_blender_frame.description: Get the current frame, the animation range and the frame rate (fps / fps_base).

set_blender_frame_range.name: set_blender_frame_range
set_blender_frame_range.title: Set Blender Frame Range
set_blender_frame_range.description: Set the animation frame range; start may equal end for a one-frame range. An unbaked rigid-body cache follows it; a baked one keeps its range, with a warning.

frame_start.description: Start frame of the animation range, 0..1048574.

frame_end.description: End frame of the animation range, 0..1048574; may equal frame_start for a one-frame range.

play_blender_animation.name: play_blender_animation
play_blender_animation.title: Play Blender Animation
play_blender_animation.description: Play, reverse, pause or stop animation playback; repeating a call changes nothing more. pause keeps the current frame, stop returns to the frame playback started from. Needs Blender's event loop: refused in background mode.

action.description: play (forward), reverse, pause (stop on the current frame) or stop (stop and return to the frame playback started from).

insert_blender_keyframe.name: insert_blender_keyframe
insert_blender_keyframe.title: Insert Blender Keyframe
insert_blender_keyframe.description: Insert a keyframe on an object property: its current value, or value; optionally the interpolation and key type.

value.description: Value to key instead of the current one: one number for a single channel (index >= 0, or a property that is not an array), otherwise one number per element, such as [x, y, z] for location. The keyed channels then show what their F-curves give at the current frame; every other channel keeps its value.

interpolation.description: Interpolation from this key to the next (CONSTANT, LINEAR, BEZIER, SINE, QUAD, CUBIC, QUART, QUINT, EXPO, CIRC, BACK, BOUNCE or ELASTIC); None leaves Blender's choice: the previous key's on a curve that already has two keys, else the preference (Bezier by default).

keyframe_type.description: Blender's key type: KEYFRAME, BREAKDOWN, MOVING_HOLD, EXTREME, JITTER or GENERATED.

delete_blender_keyframe.name: delete_blender_keyframe
delete_blender_keyframe.title: Delete Blender Keyframe
delete_blender_keyframe.description: Delete a keyframe from an object property.

frame.description: Frame number of the keyframe to delete.

get_blender_keyframes.name: get_blender_keyframes
get_blender_keyframes.title: Get Blender Keyframes
get_blender_keyframes.description: Get keyframe summary for an object.

setup_blender_rigid_body.name: setup_blender_rigid_body
setup_blender_rigid_body.title: Setup Blender Rigid Body
setup_blender_rigid_body.description: Set up rigid body physics on a mesh object, adding the scene's rigid body world when there is none, or replace its settings. Every argument is checked first (mass >= 0.001, friction >= 0, restitution and damping 0-1), and a failure leaves the scene, world and selection unchanged. kinematic=true makes an animated body that pushes simulated ones.

object_name.description: Name of the target mesh object.

body_type.description: ACTIVE (simulated) or PASSIVE (static or animated collider).

collision_shape.description: BOX, SPHERE, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, CONE, CONVEX_HULL, MESH or COMPOUND (a compound of the children's shapes).

linear_damping.description: Fraction of linear velocity lost per second, 0-1.

angular_damping.description: Fraction of angular velocity lost per second, 0-1.

kinematic.description: Animated: the body follows its own animation and pushes simulated bodies instead of being simulated.

collision_margin.description: Collision margin in meters, 0-1; omitted keeps Blender's automatic margin for a new body.

collision_collections.description: Collision collections (0-19) the body is in; bodies collide only when they share one. A new body is in 0.

use_deactivation.description: Let the body go to sleep when it nearly stops.

start_deactivated.description: Start asleep until something hits it (needs use_deactivation).

add_blender_force_field.name: add_blender_force_field
add_blender_force_field.title: Add Blender Force Field
add_blender_force_field.description: Add a force field to the scene, oriented in world space: its local +Z (where WIND blows, the axis VORTEX turns about) points along direction, world +Z by default, whatever the editor's Align preference. The reply reports rotation_euler and direction.

field_type.description: FORCE, WIND, VORTEX, MAGNET, HARMONIC, CHARGE, LENNARDJ, TEXTURE, GUIDE, BOID, TURBULENCE, DRAG or FLUID.

location.description: World-space XYZ location; the world origin when omitted.

name.description: Optional name for the field object.

direction.description: World-space direction of the field's local +Z axis.

shape.description: POINT, LINE, PLANE, SURFACE or POINTS.

flow.description: Air flow: how strongly the field also drags toward its speed.

falloff_power.description: How fast the field weakens with distance, 0-10.

distance_max.description: Distance past which the field has no effect; 0 or omitted for no limit.

get_blender_force_field_info.name: get_blender_force_field_info
get_blender_force_field_info.title: Get Blender Force Field Info
get_blender_force_field_info.description: Get force field parameters, world location and direction (local +Z) for an object; an object without a force field, such as a collider, is an error.

object_name.description: Name of the force field object.

add_blender_rigid_body_constraint.name: add_blender_rigid_body_constraint
add_blender_rigid_body_constraint.title: Add Blender Rigid Body Constraint
add_blender_rigid_body_constraint.description: Add a rigid body constraint between two different rigid bodies, as an empty at the pivot (location, default midway between them). axis sets the constraint axis in world space: the hinge axis for HINGE, the slide or motor axis for SLIDER, PISTON and MOTOR; unrotated by default, so a HINGE turns about world Z. limits, springs, motor_* and breaking_threshold configure it. Everything is checked first; a failure leaves no empty behind. The reply reports pivot, axis and local_axes.

constraint_type.description: FIXED, POINT, HINGE, SLIDER, PISTON, GENERIC, GENERIC_SPRING or MOTOR.

location.description: World-space pivot; midway between the two objects' origins when omitted.

disable_collisions.description: Disable collisions between the two objects.

axis.description: World-space direction of the constraint's axis: the hinge axis (local Z) for HINGE, the slide or motor axis (local X) for SLIDER, PISTON and MOTOR, local Z for the other types. Omitted, the empty is unrotated: a HINGE turns about world Z (a door, not a pendulum) and a SLIDER moves along world X.

limits.description: Limits by local axis, as [lower, upper] (meters for lin_*, radians for ang_*, within +-2 pi): ang_z for HINGE, lin_x for SLIDER, lin_x and ang_x for PISTON, any of lin_x, lin_y, lin_z, ang_x, ang_y, ang_z for GENERIC and GENERIC_SPRING.

springs.description: GENERIC_SPRING only: springs by local axis (x, y, z, ang_x, ang_y, ang_z), each {"stiffness": ..., "damping": ...}.

motor_angular_velocity.description: MOTOR only: target angular velocity about local X, rad/s. Blender drives object1 relative to object2, so with object1 the anchor a positive velocity turns object2 the negative way about the axis (-1.91 rad in 23 frames at +2 rad/s on Blender 5.0.1); swap the objects or the sign to reverse it.

motor_angular_max_impulse.description: MOTOR only: most impulse the angular motor applies per step (Blender's default 1).

motor_linear_velocity.description: MOTOR only: target velocity along local X, m/s, with the same convention: with object1 the anchor, object2 moves against the sign (-0.91 m in 23 frames at +1 m/s).

motor_linear_max_impulse.description: MOTOR only: most impulse the linear motor applies per step (Blender's default 1).

breaking_threshold.description: Impulse that breaks the constraint; omitted, it never breaks.

get_blender_constraint_info.name: get_blender_constraint_info
get_blender_constraint_info.title: Get Blender Constraint Info
get_blender_constraint_info.description: Get rigid body constraint info for a constraint empty: its bodies, pivot, axis and local axes in world space, limits, springs, motor and breaking threshold.

object_name.description: Name of the constraint empty object.

get_blender_physics_state.name: get_blender_physics_state
get_blender_physics_state.title: Get Blender Physics State
get_blender_physics_state.description: Get an object's world pose and rigid-body state at the current frame. An unbaked simulation advances one frame at a time, so after a frame jump a body sits where it was last simulated: by default the scene first steps from the cache start to the current frame, as playback would (up to 400 000 body-frames). pose_source and simulated_for_frame say whether the pose is the simulation's for this frame; frames past the cache end hold the bodies at its last frame (past_cache_end). rigid_body_cache reports the cache range and bake state.

step_simulation.description: Step an unbaked rigid-body simulation from its cache start to the current frame before reading the pose, at most frames x bodies = 400 000; false reads the pose as it is.

get_blender_object_trajectory.name: get_blender_object_trajectory
get_blender_object_trajectory.title: Get Blender Object Trajectory
get_blender_object_trajectory.description: Sample an object's world pose over a frame range. Not read-only: it steps the scene through the frames (frame-change handlers run, an unbaked rigid-body cache fills) and restores the current frame afterwards.

object_name.description: Name of the object to track.

end_frame.description: Last frame of trajectory (inclusive); not before start_frame.

bake_blender_simulation.name: bake_blender_simulation
bake_blender_simulation.title: Bake Blender Simulation
bake_blender_simulation.description: Bake the physics simulation for frame_start-frame_end (start before end), replacing an earlier bake: the simulation restarts from frame_start with the bodies' current transforms. scope 'rigid_body' (default) bakes only the rigid-body world's cache; 'all' bakes every point cache (rigid bodies, cloth, soft bodies, dynamic paint, particles). Refused for a disabled rigid body world. The reply gives the range the cache holds and warns about scene frames it leaves out, where bodies hold their pose. A bake runs on Blender's main thread and cannot be stopped, so one over 20 000 frames or 400 000 body-frames (frames x bodies, up to about 16 s) is refused unless allow_long_bake=true; past the client timeout Blender keeps baking and the next calls wait behind it.

frame_end.description: Last frame to bake; after frame_start.

scope.description: rigid_body bakes the rigid-body world's cache only (stepping each frame, then marking the cache baked), leaving cloth and other caches as they are; all frees and bakes every point cache in the scene, as Blender's Bake All Dynamics does: rigid bodies, cloth, soft bodies and dynamic paint over frame_start-frame_end, particle systems over the range their emission settings give.

allow_long_bake.description: Bake even above 20 000 frames or 400 000 body-frames (frames x bodies), which can outlast the client's timeout while Blender keeps baking.

free_blender_bake.name: free_blender_bake
free_blender_bake.title: Free Blender Bake
free_blender_bake.description: Free baked physics simulation data over the same scope as bake_blender_simulation ('rigid_body' by default, or 'all'). A freed cache gets the scene's frame range back, so the simulation is not cut off at the last bake's end frame. freed lists the caches that were baked.

scope.description: rigid_body frees the rigid-body world's cache only; all frees every point cache in the scene (rigid bodies, cloth, soft bodies, dynamic paint, particles).

get_blender_rigid_body_world.name: get_blender_rigid_body_world
get_blender_rigid_body_world.title: Get Blender Rigid Body World
get_blender_rigid_body_world.description: Get the scene's rigid body world: enabled, scene gravity, substeps, solver iterations, time scale, split impulse, body and constraint counts, and the cache range and bake state (rigid_body_cache). Bodies hold their pose past the cache end; warnings name a disabled world or a cache that leaves out part of the scene range.

set_blender_rigid_body_world.name: set_blender_rigid_body_world
set_blender_rigid_body_world.title: Set Blender Rigid Body World
set_blender_rigid_body_world.description: Change the scene's rigid body world, adding one when there is none; only the given settings change. gravity is the scene's, shared with cloth, soft bodies and particles. A baked cache keeps playing its bake (changed settings apply after free_blender_bake and a new bake), and its range cannot change until freed. Replies like get_blender_rigid_body_world.

enabled.description: Run the simulation; a disabled world leaves bodies at their own transforms.

gravity.description: Scene gravity [x, y, z] in m/s^2, shared with cloth, soft bodies and particles; Blender's default is [0, 0, -9.81].

time_scale.description: Simulation speed relative to the scene's frame rate, 0-100.

use_split_impulse.description: Reduce extra velocity from penetration recovery.

execute_blender_script.name: execute_blender_script
execute_blender_script.title: Execute Blender Script
execute_blender_script.description: Execute arbitrary Python code inside Blender with access to bpy. Assign to __result__ to return a value. Printed output comes back in output, cut to its first max_output_chars characters (default 32000, at most 100000), or earlier when they exceed 300000 bytes of JSON (heavily non-ASCII output); a cut sets output_truncated=true and output_total_chars to the full length. Write larger results to a file and return its path instead. Anything the script raises, including SystemExit from sys.exit(), is reported in error and never ends Blender. In attached mode each call is one undo step.

timeout.description: Maximum wall-clock seconds to wait for the script; ``None`` waits for it to finish.

max_output_chars.description: Most characters of printed output to return, 1 to 100000 (default 32000). Longer output is cut to its first max_output_chars characters with output_truncated=true and output_total_chars set. Output that JSON escapes heavily (non-ASCII text, control characters) is cut earlier, at 300000 bytes of JSON, so the prefix always arrives. Write larger results to a file and return its path instead.

create_blender_mesh_from_data.name: create_blender_mesh_from_data
create_blender_mesh_from_data.title: Create Blender Mesh From Data
create_blender_mesh_from_data.description: Create a mesh object from raw vertex, edge, and face data. Use for procedural geometry. Each vertex is exactly [x, y, z] finite numbers; a face repeating a vertex or another face's vertex set, an edge joining a vertex to itself or repeating another, and a collection outside the current scene are refused before anything is created. The mesh is validated, and a failed call leaves no mesh or object behind.

vertices.description: Vertex positions, each exactly [x, y, z] finite numbers.

edges.description: Loose edges as [v0, v1] pairs of two different vertices; face edges are made from the faces.

faces.description: Faces as lists of three or more vertex indices, each vertex once and each vertex set once.

collection_name.description: Target collection in the current scene (the scene collection if None).

clean_blender_mesh.name: clean_blender_mesh
clean_blender_mesh.title: Clean Blender Mesh
clean_blender_mesh.description: Repair a Blender mesh object's data. Always validates it, removing faces that repeat a vertex and duplicate faces or edges (geometry that can freeze Decimate); then optionally merges vertices within merge_distance, dissolves edges and faces smaller than dissolve_degenerate_distance, and recalculates normals to point outside. Reports the counts before and after. Shared mesh data changes for every object using it. Requires Object Mode.

object_name.description: Mesh object whose data to clean.

merge_distance.description: Merge vertices within this distance; None skips it.

dissolve_degenerate_distance.description: Dissolve edges and faces smaller than this; None skips it.

recalculate_normals.description: Make face normals point consistently outside.

uv_unwrap_blender_mesh.name: uv_unwrap_blender_mesh
uv_unwrap_blender_mesh.title: Uv Unwrap Blender Mesh
uv_unwrap_blender_mesh.description: Generate UV coordinates for every face of a Blender mesh object, hidden ones included, as image textures need: SMART_PROJECT (Smart UV Project: islands split at angle_limit, packed with island_margin) or CUBE_PROJECT (each face projected onto the cube side it faces). Writes uv_map_name (created when missing), else the active UV map, else a new UVMap; the active UV map stays as it was, and the reply names the render UV map, the one textures read. Enters Edit Mode briefly and restores the mesh's selection and hidden faces, the object selection and the active object. Requires Object Mode.

uv_map_name.description: UV map to write; the active one (or a new UVMap) if omitted.

angle_limit.description: SMART_PROJECT: island angle in radians, above 0 to pi/2.

cube_size.description: CUBE_PROJECT: size of the projection cube, above 0.

apply_simready_metadata.name: apply_simready_metadata
apply_simready_metadata.title: Apply Simready Metadata
apply_simready_metadata.description: Store NVIDIA SimReady metadata (semantic labels, physics properties, material info) on a Blender object as simready_ custom properties, which export_simready_usd writes as UsdPhysics and UsdSemantics schemas. Omitted fields keep their stored value; clear removes stored values. An additional label named after a field's taxonomy (class, hierarchy, wikidata_qcode) sets that field. Unknown fields, invalid values, Edit Mode and linked objects are refused, before anything changes.

anyOf.description:
Combined SimReady metadata for an asset.

Groups semantic, physics, and material properties into a single model
that is stored as Blender custom properties with a ``simready_`` prefix
and written by export_simready_usd.

Semantic labeling for SimReady assets.

export_simready_usd writes each field as a UsdSemantics LabelsAPI taxonomy
(``class``, ``hierarchy``, ``wikidata_qcode``, and each additional label's
key), or with Isaac Sim's SemanticsAPI convention where Blender's USD has
no UsdSemantics. Validation requires a label of some taxonomy on each mesh
or an exported object above it.

additional_labels.description: Custom labels such as sku or product_id; each key becomes a semantics taxonomy, so it must be an identifier. A key that is a field's taxonomy (class, hierarchy, wikidata_qcode, or the older qcode) sets that field instead, and must not disagree with it

anyOf.description:
Physics properties for SimReady assets.

export_simready_usd writes them as UsdPhysics schemas: RigidBodyAPI,
MassAPI, CollisionAPI with a MeshCollisionAPI approximation on the meshes,
and a physics material (UsdPhysics.MaterialAPI) bound with the physics
purpose. collider_type and the friction values also apply to meshes below
the object that set none of their own.

collider_type.description: UsdPhysics mesh collision approximation: convexHull, convexDecomposition, meshSimplification, none (the triangle mesh), boundingCube or boundingSphere; also mesh, box, sphere and capsule (written as none, boundingCube, boundingSphere and convexHull)

is_rigid_body.description: Whether the object is a rigid body; false clears an earlier true

anyOf.description:
Material properties for SimReady assets.

Stored as metadata only: export_simready_usd keeps them as userProperties
attributes; no USD schema carries them.

substrate_type.description: Physical substrate, e.g. metal, wood, plastic, glass, rubber, fabric, ceramic, concrete, stone

shader_type.description: Target shader, e.g. OmniPBR, OmniGlass, SimPBR

texel_density.description: Target texel density in pixels per meter

clear.description: Stored values to remove: field names such as mass_kg, a group (semantic, physics, material), additional_labels, or all.

get_simready_metadata.name: get_simready_metadata
get_simready_metadata.title: Get Simready Metadata
get_simready_metadata.description: Read NVIDIA SimReady metadata from a Blender object: semantic labels, physics properties and material info stored as simready_ custom properties. Stored values that break the rules are listed in invalid_values instead of failing the call.

validate_simready_compliance.name: validate_simready_compliance
validate_simready_compliance.title: Validate Simready Compliance
validate_simready_compliance.description: Validate the Blender objects export_simready_usd would export against the SimReady Robotics-Prop rules and Isaac Sim's asset checks; any error makes them non-compliant. Errors: an asset root that is not the identity, a rigid body skewed in the world, no material, no semantic label on a mesh or an exported object above it, invalid stored values, a rigid body without mass, without a collider or nested in another with no joint, a constraint the export cannot write as a joint (MOTOR), degenerate faces. Warnings: names, sizes and units, scaled parts, an empty slot faces use, missing colliders, what a joint leaves out, UVs, n-gons. Filter by severity and page with offset/limit (next_offset).

object_names.description: Objects to check, each with its descendants unless include_children is false. Null checks the scene's objects that are visible in renders. An empty list is refused.

check_naming.description: Validate object, material and mesh-data names.

check_scale.description: Validate real-world size in the scene's units.

check_transforms.description: Validate the asset root's and the parts' transforms.

check_metadata.description: Validate semantic labels, colliders and stored values.

check_physics.description: Validate rigid bodies (mass, colliders, nesting) and the joints their constraints become.

check_geometry.description: Validate UVs, n-gons and degenerate faces.

include_children.description: Also check the descendants of the listed objects.

severity.description: Return all issues, or only error or warning issues.

offset.description: Index of the first issue returned.

limit.description: Most issues returned (1 to 500); next_offset gives the next page.

export_simready_usd.name: export_simready_usd
export_simready_usd.title: Export Simready Usd
export_simready_usd.description: Export Blender objects as a SimReady USD asset a simulator reads: from the simready_ metadata it authors UsdPhysics rigid bodies, mass, mesh colliders and physics materials, and UsdSemantics labels; rigid body constraints between exported objects become UsdPhysics joints (fixed, revolute, prismatic, spherical, D6 with limits). The asset root is the default prim and holds its materials and joints; metersPerUnit follows the scene's Unit Scale. Listed objects export with their descendants, hidden ones too; lights, cameras and the World are left out by default. Refuses when validation finds errors; skip_checks leaves a check out, force=true ignores every error. Returns each object's prim path.

object_names.description: Objects to export, each with its descendants unless include_children is false; listed objects are exported even when hidden. Null exports the scene's objects that are visible in renders. An empty list is refused.

embed_metadata.description: Also keep the simready_ custom properties (and Blender's names) as userProperties attributes, which Blender's USD import reads back as custom properties.

validate_before_export.description: First run every validate_simready_compliance check on the exported objects, the asset root included, after writing Edit Mode's edits back to the mesh.

include_children.description: Export the descendants of the listed objects.

include_lights_and_cameras.description: Also export lights, cameras and the World's dome light, which are left out of an asset by default.

skip_checks.description: Validation checks to leave out (naming, scale, transforms, materials, hierarchy, metadata, physics, geometry), so that one check that does not apply does not need force, which also lets every other error through.

setup_simready_hierarchy.name: setup_simready_hierarchy
setup_simready_hierarchy.title: Setup Simready Hierarchy
setup_simready_hierarchy.description: Put Blender objects under a SimReady root empty (an Xform in the USD), keeping where they are, also for objects in excluded collections, skewed by a parent or under constraints. Only listed objects without a listed ancestor are re-parented; existing nesting stays. Needs Object Mode; refuses linked objects. Checks everything first and changes nothing on failure; an existing root name is refused unless reuse_root=true. Optionally stores semantic labels on the root.

root_name.description: Name for the root empty: a USD identifier (letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit).

child_names.description: Existing objects to put under the root.

anyOf.description:
Semantic labeling for SimReady assets.

export_simready_usd writes each field as a UsdSemantics LabelsAPI taxonomy
(``class``, ``hierarchy``, ``wikidata_qcode``, and each additional label's
key), or with Isaac Sim's SemanticsAPI convention where Blender's USD has
no UsdSemantics. Validation requires a label of some taxonomy on each mesh
or an exported object above it.

additional_labels.description: Custom labels such as sku or product_id; each key becomes a semantics taxonomy, so it must be an identifier. A key that is a field's taxonomy (class, hierarchy, wikidata_qcode, or the older qcode) sets that field instead, and must not disagree with it

semantic.description: Semantic labels to store on the root.

reuse_root.description: Put the objects under an existing empty named root_name; without it, an existing object of that name is refused.
